finding: Textbook Reciprocal Rank Fusion silently destroyed cross-lingual retrieval on an English-heavy corpus.
query: Why did the CFO object to the payback period?
cause: RRF sums reciprocal ranks across both lists, assuming both retrievers could rank any document. A Hindi or Arabic chunk can never appear in a BM25 list for an English query because it shares no tokens, so it collected roughly half the fused score of any English chunk BM25 ranked for any reason.

before.fusion: sum of reciprocal ranks over both arms

unrelated_english_control.text: The marketing team prefers bright packaging for summer drinks.

before.consequence: the translations of the exact query ranked below a passage about summer drinks, and nothing failed

after.fusion: mean of reciprocal ranks over ELIGIBLE arms; a chunk sharing no query token is not BM25-eligible

principle: An arm that structurally cannot express an opinion about a document must not be counted as having voted against it.
verification: The regression test was confirmed to fail with textbook RRF restored ('a translation of the exact query fell out of the top 4: [en, en, en, en]') and pass with the fix.
